name: Text Field
hint: Type an email, then tab away.
description: Text input with a floating label (or a static one above the box, to match the rest of a form), validation on blur (never while typing), a gentle shake on error, a check when valid, optional leading icon and character counter.
usage: Use for any single-line text entry: email, name, search, URL, phone, a password to sign in with. For several lines use Textarea. Give it `label` (or `aria-label` when there is no visible label), `name` and `autoComplete` so forms and autofill work, and `value` + `onChange` if you own the state. Pick the validate rule that matches the data (or pass your own function); validation runs on blur, then live once an error shows. Show a server-side error with `error`. The ref is the <input>, so `ref.current.focus()` works; unknown props (aria-*, data-*, onKeyDown) go to the <input>. A <form> reset puts it back to `defaultValue`. No success text unless you pass `successText`; `showSuccess={false}` also drops the check (useful when a valid email must not read as 'account exists'). To create a password use Password Field. The label floats inside the box by default; in a form that also has Password Field, Textarea or Tag Input, give every field the same `labelPlacement` ("above" matches their defaults) so the form reads as one design. Bump `revealErrors` on every submit so the field shakes again even when the error message has not changed.

keyboard.does: Moves focus into the input; leaving it checks the value and shows any error.
Types into the input; once an error shows, it clears or changes as you type.

screenReader: A text input named by `label`. The hint, error or success line is linked with aria-describedby and read in a live region (assertive for an error), and an error sets aria-invalid. With `maxLength` the count is part of the description, read as "n of max characters" (`messages.count`) when the field takes focus.

dataProps.description: Visible label. "" for none (then pass aria-label).

"float": the label sits inside a 56px box and floats up on focus or once there is a value. "above": a static label over a 48px box (52px on phones and touch), as Password Field, Textarea and Tag Input draw it by default. Give every field in a form the same value so the labels read as one design.
Input type: "email" | "text" | "url" | "tel" | "password" | "search" | "number" (any <input> type works).
Help line under the box. An error or success message replaces it while it shows.

Leading icon (18px, --ts-ink2): any name from the kit's icon set, or "none". The gallery offers five; every name works: check, x, plus, minus, chevronRight, chevronDown, chevronLeft, chevronUp, arrowRight, arrowLeft, arrowDown, copy, heart, share, bookmark, message, more, trash, search, settings, bell, image, link, edit, sparkle, bold, italic, camera, doc, upload, user, users, calendar, lock, eye, eyeOff, star, mail, mailOpen, alert, sun, moon, home, folder, inbox, chart, grid, layers, globe, book, code, menu, panel, zap, box, help, logout, play, pause, skipForward, shuffle, music, radio, pin, phone, navigation, flag, archive, clock, refresh, coffee.
Character limit. Shows the n/max counter (unless showCount is false), turns it red when over and shows the tooLong error after blur. Never cuts the text. 0 = no limit.
Controlled value: pass it with onChange and the field shows exactly this. Leave undefined to let the field keep its own (seeded by defaultValue).
Initial value when uncontrolled. A <form> reset returns to it.
(value: string) => void, on every keystroke (and on form reset).
(event) => void, after the field marks itself touched and validates.
(event) => void.
Forwarded to the <input>: focus(), select(), measure.
id of the <input>. Generated when omitted.
Form field name; the <input> carries the value in FormData.
autocomplete token ("email", "name", "current-password", "one-time-code"…). Defaults by type: email→email, tel→tel, url→url, password→current-password; otherwise unset.
Virtual-keyboard hint ("numeric", "decimal", "email", "tel", "search", "url").
Focus the input on mount.
Shown inside the box once the label has floated (or always when there is no label).
Marks the input required (native constraint and aria) and adds * to the label. With validate="none" it also applies the required rule.
Value can be read and selected but not edited.
Not focusable, dimmed, left out of FormData.
An error you already have (for example from the server). Shown as the field's error until you clear it; the box shakes once when it appears (bump revealErrors to shake again for the same message).

dataProps.type: "email" | "required" | "url" | "none" | ((value: string, messages: { required?: string; emailRequired?: string; email?: string; urlRequired?: string; url?: string; tooLong?: string | ((max: number) => string); invalid?: string; count?: (n: number, max: number) => string }) => string | null)
dataProps.description: "email" | "required" | "url" | "none", or a function (value, messages) => string | null: return the error message, or null when the value is fine.

dataProps.type: { required?: string; emailRequired?: string; email?: string; urlRequired?: string; url?: string; tooLong?: string | ((max: number) => string); invalid?: string; count?: (n: number, max: number) => string }
dataProps.description: Copy, merged over neutral defaults: { required: "This field is required", emailRequired: "Enter your email address", email: "Enter a valid email address", urlRequired: "Enter a URL", url: "Enter a valid URL", tooLong: (max) => `Keep it under ${max} characters`, invalid: "Check this field", count: (n, max) => `${n} of ${max} characters` (the counter as screen readers hear it) }. Pass only the keys you want to change.
Message under the field once it validates. Empty by default: only the check mark shows.
Show the check mark and successText when the value passes validation. false keeps a valid field neutral.

With maxLength set, show the n/max counter on the message line (11px mono in --ts-ink2, which meets 4.5:1 in light and dark; --ts-danger when over). false keeps the length rule and the error without the counter.
Bump this on every submit (0 → 1 → 2…): marks the field touched and shakes it while anything is wrong, including an `error` you pass, so a second submit with the same message still shakes.
Widest the field grows, in px. 0 lets it fill its container.
Added to the root (the element that holds label, box and message line).
Inline style on the root.
Sample content for the gallery: success text "Looks good". Off by default.

example:
<form onSubmit={save}>
  <TextField
    ref={emailRef}
    label="Work email"
    name="email"
    autoComplete="email"
    required
    value={email}
    onChange={setEmail}
    error={serverError}
    messages={{ emailRequired: "Add an email so we can reach you" }}
    showSuccess={false}
    maxWidth={0}
  />
</form>
